summary: We discuss microgravity and the flames of fire within it, the consequences, their behavior, and we offer a solution to prevent accidents.
details:
Hello, It isolates an ignition source and test samples inside a hermetic, transparent, and resistant environment.

It uses a dosing system (with a micrometric pump and high-pressure lines) to introduce extinguishing agents such as extinguisher gas or micro-mist water in a controlled way to smother the flames.

It allows simulating and monitoring in real time critical variables such as internal pressure, gas flow, and the visual behavior of the fire.

Absolute Safety: Keeps the fire completely confined and controlled, avoiding risks during testing.

Technical Precision: Regulates the exact amount of extinguishing agent entering through pressure gauges and valves, avoiding violent discharges or waste.

High Accessibility: Features a square, removable front face with quick-release latches that make it easy to place and remove test samples comfortably.

It combines precision laboratory equipment with everyday fire safety components (fire extinguishers and quick-access latches), achieving a modular, safe, and functional test bench for millimeter-level fire containment.

We base our work on vacuum chambers and the behavior of cold fires, since without oxygen and with a non-toxic extinguisher, it can be extinguished, and we can also be sure that it won't reignite new and hurt the astronauts.
dataRefs: Larger scale flame studies have been conducted aboard Northrop Grumman Cygnus spacecraft after they depart station. This Saffire series of experiments allowed for scaled-up studies of fire spread

Microgravity is the condition in which people or objects appear to be weightless. The effects of microgravity can be seen when astronauts and objects float in space. Microgravity can be experienced in other ways, as well. “Micro-” means “very small,” so microgravity refers to the condition where gravity seems to be very small. In microgravity, astronauts can float in their spacecraft – or outside, on a spacewalk. Heavy objects move around easily. For example, astronauts can move equipment weighing hundreds of pounds with their fingertips. Microgravity is sometimes called “zero gravity,” but this is misleading.
projectRefs: Fire is one of the greatest hazards in crewed space missions. On the International Space Station (ISS), an experiment is studying flames in microgravity, using PMMA rods subjected to an opposing flow of an inert gas. Flame propagation is controlled by two heat transfer mechanisms, called the thermal regime and the chemical regime. On Earth (1g), the thermal regime dominates for slow opposing flow; however, in microgravity ( μg ), a transition between the thermal and chemical regimes is observed. This result confirms the predictions of theoretical models and allows for the validation of computer simulations of flame propagation, which are key to studying different fire prevention and suppression measures.
